briefdescription.para: Root instructions are instructions from which complex computation starts.
Topologically sorted root instructions.
When examining a basic block for complex deinterleaving, if it is a simple one-block loop, then the only incoming block is 'Incoming' and the 'BackEdge' block is the block itself.
ReductionInfo maps from ReductionOp to PHInode and Instruction OutsideUser as it is shown in the IR:

detaileddescription.para: vector.body: PHInode = phi <vector type> [ zeroinitializer, entry ], [ ReductionOp, vector.body ] ... ReductionOp = fadd i64 ... ... br i1 condition, label vector.body, middle.block
OutsideUser can be llvm.vector.reduce.fadd or fadd preceding llvm.vector.reduce.fadd when unroll factor isn't one.

briefdescription.para: In the process of detecting a reduction, we consider a pair of ReductionOP, which we refer to as real and imag (or vice versa), and traverse the use-tree to detect complex operations.

detaileddescription.para: As this is a reduction operation, it will eventually reach RealPHI and ImagPHI, which corresponds to the ReductionOPs that we suspect to be complex. RealPHI and ImagPHI are used by the identifyPHINode method.

briefdescription.para: Set this flag to true if RealPHI and ImagPHI were reached during reduction detection.
OldToNewPHI maps the original real PHINode to a new, double-sized PHINode.

detaileddescription.para: The new PHINode corresponds to a vector of deinterleaved complex numbers. This mapping is populated during ComplexDeinterleavingOperation::ReductionPHI node replacement. It is then used in the ComplexDeinterleavingOperation::ReductionOperation node replacement process.

briefdescription.para: If the code is compiled with -Ofast or expressions have reassoc flag, the order of complex computation operations may be significantly altered, and the real and imaginary parts may not be executed in parallel.

detaileddescription.para: This function takes this into consideration and employs a more general approach to identify complex computations. Initially, it gathers all the addends and multiplicands and then constructs a complex expression from them.

briefdescription.para: Identifies the Deinterleave operation applied to a vector containing complex numbers.

detaileddescription.para:
There are two ways to represent the Deinterleave operation:
Using two shufflevectors with even indices for /pReal instruction and odd indices for /pImag instructions (only for fixed-width vectors)
Using two extractvalue instructions applied to vector.deinterleave2 intrinsic (for both fixed and scalable vectors)

briefdescription.para: identifying the operation that represents a complex number repeated in a Splat vector.

detaileddescription.para: There are two possible types of splats: ConstantExpr with the opcode ShuffleVector and ShuffleVectorInstr. Both should have an initialization mask with all values set to zero.
